title: Achieving bio-protection in New Zealand ecosystems mesocosm fungal pathogen OTU table
author: Waller, Lauren
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-zero

steps.title: Set up mesocosm pots
steps.instruction: Prepare 80 mesocosms using 125 L pots (575 mm diameter) for the experiment.

steps.title: Assemble plant communities
steps.instruction: Create 20 unique eight‑species plant communities, varying orthogonally in exotic species proportion (0‑100 %) and woody shrub/tree proportion (0‑63 %). Choose species from a pool of 20 exotic and 19 native/endemic New Zealand plants.

steps.title: Condition soil biota
steps.instruction: Grow each of the eight representative plant species in monoculture in 10 L pots containing field‑collected soil for 9‑10 months to condition typical associated soil biota.

steps.title: Create home‑soil inoculum
steps.instruction: For each mesocosm, collect the conditioned soil from its eight resident plant species and mix them together to form a single ‘home’ soil inoculum.

steps.title: Apply inocula to mesocosms
steps.instruction: Introduce each ‘home’ soil mixture into its corresponding mesocosm (home treatment) and also into a different mesocosm that lacks any of the eight representative plant species (away treatment).

steps.title: Grow mesocosms
steps.instruction: Allow the planted mesocosms to grow for approximately one year under experimental conditions.

steps.title: Harvest plants and sample roots
steps.instruction: After the growth period, harvest all plants from each mesocosm and collect root samples from every individual plant (total n = 491).

steps.title: Extract DNA from roots
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from each root sample using an appropriate plant DNA extraction method.

steps.title: Sequence fungal DNA
steps.instruction: Sequence the fungal DNA from the extracted root DNA using a suitable high‑throughput sequencing platform.

steps.title: Cluster sequences into OTUs
steps.instruction: Pair the fungal sequences and cluster them into operational taxonomic units (OTUs) at 97 % similarity.

steps.title: Assign pathogen functional attributes
steps.instruction: Assign functional attributes to the OTUs using the FUNGUILD database and retain only those taxa classified as “probable” or “highly probable” plant pathogens.
